message.content:
To terminate Visual Studio Code from the command line (Windows), you can use the built‑in **`taskkill`** utility:

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

Explanation of the switches:

| Switch | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `/IM`  | Specifies the image name (process executable) – here `code.exe`. |
| `/F`   | Forces termination (`/T` would also terminate child processes). |

If you only want to target a specific instance (e.g., one window), you’ll need its process ID (PID) first:

```cmd
tasklist | findstr code.exe          # Find the PID(s)
taskkill /PID <pid> /F               # Kill that particular PID
```

**Notes**

* Running `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` will close *all* running instances of VS Code, so make sure you’ve saved your work beforehand.
* If you’re on PowerShell, you can achieve the same with:
  
  ```powershell
  Stop-Process -Name code -Force
  ```

That’s all you need to force‑close VS Code from the command prompt.
